args.title: Patent Representation Learning via Self-supervision
args.summary:
Investigates whether patent embeddings can be learned fully self-supervised, without citation or IPC labels, by treating different sections of the same patent (abstract, claims, background, description) as complementary contrastive views, replacing dropout-based augmentation which the paper shows causes patent-specific over-dispersion (loss of semantic cohesion). On a 200-query prior-art retrieval task, section-based augmentation raises Recall@100 from 56.21 to 71.22 using claims as the second view, matching or surpassing the citation-trained PAECTER baseline at several cutoffs. On IPC-subclass classification (30k USPTO patents, HUPD split), it performs on par with or better than the much larger gte-Qwen2-7B-instruct model. The result is a label-free route to patent embeddings competitive with citation-supervised baselines, of particular interest where citation signal is sparse.

key_facts: Section-based augmentation (different patent sections as contrastive views) replaces SimCSE-style dropout augmentation, which causes patent-specific over-dispersion (loss of semantic cohesion).
Prior-art retrieval (200 queries, Claims-to-All setting): R@100 rises from 56.21 to 71.22 with section-based augmentation using claims as the second view.
Section-augmented retrieval matches or surpasses citation-trained PAECTER at several cutoffs despite using no citation supervision.

IPC subclass classification (KNN k=10, 30k USPTO patents 2005-2009, HUPD 85/15 split): section-based augmentation performs on par with or better than gte-Qwen2-7B-instruct despite far fewer parameters.
Different patent sections specialize for different tasks; section-augmented models retrieve a more balanced section mix, indicating improved cross-structure generalization.
